articleTitle: BART Fine Tuning based Abstractive Summarization of Patients Medical Questions Texts
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Today, many people get counseling about their problems by interviewing doctors or communicating via online platforms. With neural architectures such as Transformer achieving high-performance results in the field of natural language processing, the use of these approaches has become quite common in solving many natural language processing problems in the medical field. In this study, a method using BART (Bidirectional Auto-Regressive Transformer) neural architecture is proposed for abstractive summarization of questions asked by patients to doctors. In the proposed method, the pretrained BART neural architecture is retrained using a dataset consisting of questions asked by patients to doctors and summaries of these questions. The evaluation of the summary questions obtained was carried out with the ROUGE metric and compared with other approaches in the literature from different perspectives. When the comparative results are examined, the ROUGE performance of our approach is higher than 92% of other studies that use abstractive medical summary.

articleTitle: User Feedback-based Approach for Identifying the Influential Features of the "Man of the Match" Award
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The "Man of the Match" award in sports has always been a subject of interest and debate. To better understand the important characteristics that contribute to qualification as a "Man of the Match," this research paper presents a user feedback-based approach by involving more than 100 individuals of varying ages, genders, and backgrounds. The study aims to perform feature selection by analyzing the reviews given by these individuals after observing sports matches. This approach is versatile and these features are adaptable and can be utilized in any cricket format. Various feature extraction techniques are applied to uncover the most influential attributes that lead to the recognition of a player as the "Man of the Match." The outcomes of this study provide important insights into the subjective perception of excellent sports achievements.

articleTitle: Soil Classification and Crop Yield Prediction using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: India, known for its agricultural landscape, is a prominent producer of numerous crops globally. Despite being at the center of the agricultural industry, Indian farmers are often relegated to the bottom of the social hierarchy. The task of identifying which crop is most appropriate and successful for a particular type of soil remains a challenge, as soil types vary across different geographic regions. Though few technological solutions exist to address this problem, farmers still face difficulty in making informed decisions. To overcome this challenge, this paper presents a crop recommendation system that chooses the best crop to be cultivated using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Random Forest model. The method can produce precise forecasts by examining a number of variables, including the region, soil type, area to be grown, and season.

articleTitle: Unmasking Comic Narratives: CNN-RF Approach to Genre Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Classifying comic genres is challenging in computer vision and image analysis, with broad implications for image retrieval, comic book cataloguing, and content recommendation. In this study, the authors provide a novel approach designed for the automatic genre categorization of comic pictures. Our method aims to accomplish accurate and complex genre identification using the powerful synergy between Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and a Random Forest (RF) classifier. Carefully calculated for every genre category, important metrics are used to assess the model's performance: precision, recall, F1-score, support, and overall accuracy. The testing results show impressive skill, exhibiting high categorization accuracy in all genres. With a 98% accuracy rate overall, this is rather outstanding. More specifically, the model performs very well in accuracy, recall, and F1 scores for the Humor, Battle, and Love Fantasy genres, repeatedly exceeding 90% in these critical measures. Interestingly, the genres of Science Fiction, Romance, Horror, Action, and Science Fiction all do well in terms of categorization, with F1 scores that often above 90%. The CNN- RF model has shown a strong and all-encompassing performance that highlights its potential to transform the automation of comic genre categorization tasks.

articleTitle: Autoencoder Based Method for Detection of Steel Wire Defects
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: In the steel industry, quality control of the final product is usually done by manual visual inspection. Due to the disadvantages of manual visual inspection, research and development of new automatic inspection techniques for the detection of steel surface defects has gained more importance in recent years. The development of industrial processes and the need for new systems have revealed new defect detection methods based on computer vision. The importance of automatic inspection based on computer vision is based on its adoption as a quality control tool, which can inspect without damaging the material to be examined and without affecting the production speed. In this context, it is the main objective of the manufacturers that the inspection to be applied during steel production solves the tasks of the people currently carrying out the inspection work with an automatic inspection system. In this study, an autoencoder based defect detection method is proposed for the detection of steel wire defects. In the study, the defects on the steel were detected by using a deep automatic encoder. In autoencoders, abnormal data produces higher rendering error than normal data. This situation is used to detect abnormal situations in images. Using this method, an accuracy rate of 94.44% was obtained in classifying the anomalies on the steel surface.

articleTitle: DINE PASS: Improving Hostel Dining Experience using Sense-Think-Act Paradigm
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The traditional dining experience, in college mess halls has long been plagued by problems such as inefficiencies, long lines, lower personal hygienic practices and manual record keeping. To tackle these issues a solution called "Dine Pass" is introduced in this paper. Dine Pass aims to revolutionize hostel dining entry experience by leveraging technology and a smart approach to streamline and enhance every aspect of the dining journey. By utilizing sensors like RFID readers and IR sensors Dine Pass establishes an automated authentication system that eliminates the need for paper-based mess cards and time-consuming manual checks. With a tap of their RFID card students can swiftly access the mess hall without facing long queues or wasting time. In addition to improving entry efficiency Dine Pass also addresses hygiene concerns by incorporating a hand sanitizer dispenser triggered by IR sensors. This ensures cleanliness. This paper highlights the challenges and inefficiencies associated with the existing system such, as time consuming processes, infection risks and ineffective record keeping. The proposed Dine Pass system provides an integrated solution to overcome these issues. By implementing automated authentication processes implementing hygiene measures and ensuring accuracy, in record keeping Dine Pass greatly enhances the overall dining experience at hostels. Through the implementation of Dine Pass, institutions stand to benefit from increased operational efficiency, reduced queue times, improved hygiene standards, and enhanced data management. Students, on the other hand, can enjoy seamless access to meals, better utilization of time, and heightened peace of mind regarding hygiene. This paper delves into the multifaceted advantages of Dine Pass and provides insights into its potential to reshape the landscape of hostel mess dining systems.

articleTitle: Recommendations for a Vertical Farming System Using Hydroponics, Machine Learning and IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Agriculture nowadays faces several problems because of the rise of the global population, which increased the food demand and caused instability in food security. Organic food that is pesticide-free is also in high demand, leading to consuming more arable lands, water, pesticides, and fossil fuels. Vertical farming is a promising solution to these challenges. It is a method of growing plants in vertically stacked layers, which can be done indoors or outdoors. Hydroponics is a method of growing plants without soil, using a nutrient-rich water solution. Vertical farming using hydroponics can solve these problems by integrating IoT and AI technology. It reduces water wastage and eliminates pesticide consumption. The aim of this research is to develop recommendations for a Vertical Farming System using hydroponic based on Machine Learning and IoT technology for a better, controlled, and monitored growth of plants. The hydroponic system and its parameters are monitored and controlled by a GUI using the Blynk app that allows the user to control the food quality by its nutrients and parameters to help in producing more organic food. Crop yield health is being predicted by an AI model that detects the healthy and unhealthy leaves with an accuracy of 82%, hence saving many farmers’ time. The system is also applicable for personal use, allowing individuals or families to plant their own food.

articleTitle: ‘Watch and Buy’ and its impact on online retailers and manufacturer: A Stackelberg and Nash game analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: ‘Watch and Buy’ or live stream (LS) selling is a novel selling method where an influencer will showcase the product through an LS channel or social media; the consumer can interact with the influencer and buy the product online. Our study, for the first time, analyses the pricing decisions of an LS channel when they competes with the traditional online retailer (OR). We also analysed the impact of LS on OR and the product manufacturer (PM). Later, we examined the effect of conversion rate and revenue sharing contract on the supply chain partners’ profit. This study’s findings can act as a starting point for the analytical studies in LS selling and can aid the management practitioners of LS, OR and PM to optimise their profit.

articleTitle: Unveiling Diabetes Predictions: Bridging Complexity and Clarity through Interpretable AI and SHAP Insights
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This research paper explores the realm of interpretable machine learning models for predicting diabetes, utilizing the PIMA Indian diabetes dataset (PIDD). With the increasing prevalence of diabetes, accurate prediction has gained paramount importance, and explainable AI offers a bridge between complex models and actionable insights. Various machine learning algorithms, such as decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting, and neural networks, are explored for predicting diabetes onset based on individual health attributes. To enhance model interpretability, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values, a powerful technique, are employed to offer transparent insights into prediction rationale. Through SHAP values, the impact of individual features on model predictions is uncovered, demystifying the decision-making process. Traditional models like decision trees inherently provide interpretability, whereas complex models like neural networks benefit from SHAP values to reveal their prediction drivers. The analysis not only identifies influential features but also aids in assessing model fairness and robustness. The results highlight the delicate balance between model complexity and transparency. This study underscores the significance of interpretability in diabetes prediction models and demonstrates SHAP value’s efficacy in unraveling intricate machine learning behaviors. As healthcare relies increasingly on artificial intelligence (AI), this research contributes to informed model selection, fostering reliable and transparent medical AI applications. By shedding light on the intricate workings of predictive models, the discourse on trustworthy and effective AI deployment in critical healthcare scenarios is advanced.

articleTitle: Sustainable & Intelligent Transportation System: The Case Study of Un-signalized Pedestrian Crossing at Stationary Bottleneck and Its Impact on Traffic Flow
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The study examines how unsignalized pedestrians affect the flow of vehicles in a stationary bottleneck. The impact of unsignalized pedestrian crossings at stationary bottlenecks is not considered by the Highway Capacity Manual (HCM), even though it offers a technique for estimating the level of service for urban roadway segments. The average travel time for vehicles along the road segment increases due to confrontations between automobiles and pedestrians at these crossings on urban roadways. As a result, as a segment's running time increases, so do the vehicle's speed and quality of service. Determine the pace of pedestrians crossing the road at a stationary bottleneck to estimate the delay this condition will generate This study's primary goal is to measure pedestrian speed and analyze how it affects traffic flow at stationary bottlenecks. The study also hopes to include its findings in the HCM's Urban Street Analysis Chapter.

articleTitle: A GAN-Based Approach to Generate Images from Text Description
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: As developments in language and visual processing progress, the need for technologies in this field has increased. Systems that produce images from text can be integrated into smart systems, so that systems can be used more effectively. These systems, known as text-to-image in the literature, have many uses. In the field of visual content production, realistic visuals can be produced by reading a text-based description or by inputting a text. In the content completion area, they can complete the missing or unclear parts of the image by taking a text-based input. A visual story can be created from a story text or a scenario by visual storytelling. Apart from such processes, synthetic data can be created by using text descriptions as well as existing images to expand visual data sets in data augmentation processes. In the fields of image search and image indexing, the text-to-image structure is used when we want to find a specific image with a specific text query. In this study, GAN architectures that produce images from text are examined and the steps of creating these architectures with cGAN are examined. As a result of the study, the Inception Score was measured as 3.22.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Heartbeat Classification of 12-Lead ECG Time Series Signal
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the most prevalent cause of mortality on a global scale. The possibility of preventing cardiac diseases is dependent on early-stage intervention. At this point, the electrocardiogram (ECG) emerges as a critical modality for detecting and predicting future cardiac abnormalities. Numerous machine-learning techniques have been used to improve result precision, computational efficiency, and model durability. Deep learning approaches have recently emerged as the preferred method for reaching even better levels of accuracy and robustness in a diverse range of applications. In this research, we developed four different neural networks. They are the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), the Artificial Neural Network (ANN), the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, and a unique hybrid LSTM-CNN network. These networks were created to evaluate the classification performance between normal and abnormal heartbeats. Our hybrid model performed exceptionally well on the test data, with a loss of 0.12, binary accuracy of 0.97%, and area under curve (AUC) score of 0.99%. The results demonstrate its ability to successfully extract local and contextual factors within ECG signals. The combination of LSTM and CNN networks in a hybrid architecture allowed our model to exploit both local and contextual information within the ECG signals.

articleTitle: Tomato Disease Classification using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Research on methods that use images to identify and categorize plant diseases is expanding as a field of study. These programs help find plant illnesses as they happen. Fungal, bacterial, and viral infections are the most harmful to plants. Five major tomato diseases have been classified in this study: Bacterial Spot, Black Mold, Gray Spot, Late Blight, Powdery Mildew, and healthy tomato plant leaf. The classification is done by extracting color, shape, and texture features from healthy and unhealthy tomato plant images. Following the segmentation phase, the feature extraction method is carried out. Features extracted from segmented pictures are used as inputs to a classification algorithm. These five categories were used to finalize the illness categorization system. The variety of five kinds of tomato images yielded an overall 98% classification accuracy. Furthermore, various research gaps have been identified to achieve a more open approach to detecting tomato diseases.

articleTitle: Investigating impact of gold and bitcoin prices on stock market
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Stock market performance is a challenging task due to high complexity and volatility in the financial markets There are many factors that influence the stock market and make it volatile. This research perform ordinary least square (OLS) to investigate the relationship between the wider Standard and Poor (S&P 500) US index, and the two independent variables, Bitcoin and gold prices. Daily time series data were collected from January 2015 to December 2022, with a total of 2011 daily observations, to determine whether gold and Bitcoin, or one of them, has a substantial impact on the S&P 500 index by using the Multiple Regression model. The results found that the S&P 500 market index is considerably impacted by both gold and Bitcoin, but gold has a larger impact on the S&P 500 Index than Bitcoin.

articleTitle: Restaurant Automation: A Framework using Data Acquisition and Visualization for Improved Customer Experiences
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Restaurants are an integral component of the culinary industry and have become a significant area of research with the advancements in technology. Incorporation of innovative approaches in the hospitality sector ensures improved efficiency, better customer experience and adaptability for evolving resources. The concept of "Restaurant Automation" has been revolutionizing the customers and restaurant proprietors experience by providing culinary excellence and world-class dining establishments. This work focuses on investigating the influence of technological interventions on customer dining experiences at the automated restaurants by developing a sensor-based solution for order-taking and processing, comprehensive customer monitoring, and table management for in-dine experiences. Through the automated ordering and processing system, customers can place their orders seamlessly, leading to quicker service and minimizing order inaccuracies. The real-time customer monitoring component empowers the restaurant staff to promptly address customer needs and preferences and encourages personalized interactions and enhancing loyalty. The automated table management system optimizes resource allocation and reduces waiting times, fostering customer satisfaction, and streamlined operations. The system is designed and implemented using Sense-Think-Act paradigm with use of data capture and visualization technologies. The proposed solution is cost-effective and energy efficient and utilizes current state-of-the-art in restaurant automation.

articleTitle: Chronic Kidney Disease Detection: A Comparative study
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a life-threatening disease that impairs the kidney making it unable to filter blood properly. Early detection and appropriate treatment of CKD are crucial to increase the survival rate of patients. This study provides a comparative analysis for the identification of CKD. Toward this end, the performance of Logistic Regression, Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), and Support Vector Machines (SVM) classifiers have been compared. The CKD dataset of the UCI machine learning repository was used to train the models. The dataset consists of 400 cases of which 246 (62%) have CKD and 149 (38%) are healthy cases. The dataset has 25 features distributed into 11 numerical features and 14 categorical features, including the response. The data were loaded into R for exploratory data analysis and pre-processing. To solve the issue of data imbalance, the researchers performed oversampling on the dataset. This study revealed that Random Forest outperforms others with an accuracy of 0.992 and 0.993 F1Score after oversampling. Additionally, the study found that oversampling increased the performance of Logistic Regression, Random Forest and SVM models. However, KNN experienced a decrease in performance after resampling, from 0.988 to 0.967 accuracy after oversampling.

articleTitle: Analyzing Tech-Driven Solutions for Overcoming Challenges in the Indian E-commerce Landscape
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The exponential expansion of the e-commerce sector in India can be attributed to factors such as digitization, shifts in consumer behavior, and advancements in technology. However, the sector’s complete potential is impeded by a myriad of problems that coincide with its growth trajectory. This study employed a methodology that comprised structured interviews, adopting purposeful sampling of 130 executives and managers in the e-commerce business. This research aims to shed light on these issues and investigate the role of potential technical solutions in resolving them. The paper dives into a variety of technical solutions such as multi-lingual artificial intelligence interfaces, blockchain technology for enhancing supply chain transparency, and secure authentication mechanisms. Technology is key to resolving payment inclusion and last-mile delivery and increasing data security and privacy. This research endeavors to offer practical recommendations for businesses, policymakers, and stakeholders by identifying obstacles and recommending solutions driven by technology. The study envisions a future in which technological interventions propel India’s e-commerce industry to new heights, fostering economic development and empowering consumers.

articleTitle: Better Usage Container Selection Algorithm for Energy Consumption Minimization in Cloud Data Centers
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: With the latest popularity gained by Container as a service (CaaS) paradigm in the cloud computing environment, most cloud providers now adopt it in executing user’s tasks. Tasks execution in this platform is like a multiple bin-packing problem where tasks are scheduled on containers; containers containing tasks are scheduled on virtual machines (VMs) and VMs are scheduled on physical machines (PMs). With this multiple layer scheduling scheme, if scheduling is not properly done, it can lead to under-utilization or over-utilization of VMs and PMs; where the containers and VMs are respectively scheduled onto. In either way, under-utilization or over-utilization of VMs and PMs result into high energy consumption in the cloud data center. Energy consumption in the CaaS paradigm need to be minimized. Container selection algorithms are used to select container(s) to be migrated from an overloaded VM, so that energy consumption in the cloud data center may be improved. This work proposed an algorithm known as Better Usage Container Selection algorithm to select container(s) to be migrated from over-loaded VM. This algorithm was compared with Maximum Usage container selection algorithm based on energy consumption, service level agreement (SLA) violation and number of container migration. Results show that when the number of containers is around 1000, the proposed algorithm minimizes energy consumption by about 9.3% on average. But, consumed about 23.3% more energy when the number of container is 4000. MU algorithm produced lesser number of container migration while there is a 27.6% SLA violation by the proposed algorithm when the number of container is less or equal to 1000, but when the number of container is 4000, MU shows a SLA violation of about 2.02%.

articleTitle: A Federated Learning Mechanism for Preserving Security of Sensitive Data
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning(ML) method which allows for model training on information distributed across various servers and devices without sharing the sensitive data. It works by aggregating updates and weight values from the devices while keeping raw data private and secure. FL is a field which is widely used in finance, healthcare, and IoT systems along with personalized recommendations. Traditional ML and deep learning (DL) models are capable of producing good outcomes, however, these algorithms do not provide data security due to directly working on the raw data. Moreover, the FL can avoid security concerns due to its behaviour of sending the model to the data instead of working on the raw data itself. In this work, the FL has been introduced along with its three kinds of architectures. The motivation behind this work is that healthcare departments and financial institutes avoid sharing patients' sensitive information due to privacy concerns. However, the ML and DL models require a vast volume of data for accurate prediction outcomes. Hence, FL has been identified as the best model for working on sensitive data without privacy concerns. Furthermore, the work has also introduced the core challenges and application areas of FL. Moreover, in future, the FL architectures will be implemented with the healthcare dataset to increase data security and efficiently identify the outcomes.

articleTitle: Talk to your data: Enhancing Business Intelligence and Inventory Management with LLM-Driven Semantic Parsing and Text-to-SQL for Database Querying
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This paper delves into the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) in revolutionizing business intelligence and inventory management through semantic parsing and text-to-SQL methodologies. It assesses various LLM models, such as DIN-SQL, DSP, NSQL, GPT, CoPilot, and LLaMa, elucidating their capabilities and contributions. Two critical analyses are presented here. The first compares cutting-edge LLM models using cosine similarity and cost efficiency metrics. The second analysis enhances GPT’s precision through prompt engineerings, like few-shot techniques, and explores frameworks like DIN-SQL, NSQL, and DSP. DIN-SQL substantially boosts accuracy, and NSQL demonstrates potential in specific scenarios. This research underscores the transformative potential of LLM-driven models in business intelligence and inventory management. DIN-SQL, in particular, emerges as a game-changer with the potential to reshape inventory management practices. GPT showcases its versatility through fine-tuning for tasks beyond conventional programming, while CoPilot offers a cost-effective alternative. This study emphasizes the importance of cost-effectiveness in real-world applications, with LLaMa and CoPilot being practical choices. NSQL, with its budget-friendly and semi-accurate solution, holds promise for semantic parsing in growing companies. These insights are a foundation for further innovation, promising unmatched efficiency and competitiveness across industries in the evolving Artificial intelligence landscape.

articleTitle: Parkinson's Disease Detection Using Data Mining Models: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Data Mining techniques have emerged in the healthcare industry over the past years in determining the occurrences and development of diseases. This paper aim is to conduct a comparative study between three Data Mining models in predicting Parkinson’s Disease using biological voice measurements dataset. The three models that are evaluated are: Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM). Data oversampling using Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) method was used to balance the data and feature selection was applied to select the most relevant attributes. The CRISP-DM framework is used to perform the analysis using Weka machine learning tool. The results showed that the KNN model obtained the best accuracy of 94.11% on balanced dataset.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Approach with EfficientNet and SE Block Attention Mechanism for Multiclass Alzheimer's Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease can be detected beforehand using brain MRI images. However, this situation requires a specialist in the field and is a very open area to human error. In addition, it takes a long time for specialist doctors to analyze images and make decisions by diagnosing diseases. In this study, it is aimed to detect Alzheimer's disease quickly and with high accuracy by using deep learning architectures. In addition, with the use of the proposed study in hospitals, it can play an important role in reducing false treatments by supporting doctors in disease detection. In the study, open source licensed brain MR images dataset obtained from Kaggle was used. The dataset is divided into 3 subgroups as training, validation and testing. Within the scope of the work, where EfficientNet-B0 architecture and SE block attention mechanisms were used, a model specific to the data set was developed and used. The results of the studies were compared with other studies using the same data set and detailed results were given in the study. Studies have shown that Brain MRI images can be successfully classified with an accuracy of 0.9903. The findings suggested that the architecture created might help reduce human error in diagnosing Alzheimer's disease.

articleTitle: Evaluating Sri Lankan Regional Electricity Demand During COVID-19 Restrictions Using VIIRS Nighttime Light Intensity: An Image-Based Statistical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The COVID-19 related lockdowns had a significant impact on mobility and economic activity around the world. This paper explores the impact of the COVID-19 lockdowns in Sri Lanka using nighttime light (NTL) intensity obtained from VIIRS satellite images between January 2019 and March 2021. The frequency and intensity images of the satellite images were normalized using the maximum and minimum pixel value of the images to obtain raster images in order to observe variations in illumination across months. The dot product of the normalized intensity and frequency images were obtained to calculate the zonal statistics. In addition to the visual representation, a panel regression analysis was used to examine the statistical impact of COVID-19 lockdowns. Results of the analysis show that the national COVID-19 lockdowns have an adverse effect on electricity consumption. However, during national COVID-19 lockdowns, changes in NTL intensity is negligible compared to electricity consumption. This can be due to Sri Lanka not being an industrial country and due to internal migration. Limitations of this study are that a short time horizon has been considered and the absence of disaggregated information on electricity consumption. Furthermore, the relationship between the economic activity of Sri Lanka with NLT intensity and electricity consumption has not been considered.

articleTitle: Knowledge and Attitude of Healthcare Providers in the United Arab Emirates about Stem Cells Biotechnology
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This work represents a cross-sectional study that is primarily aimed at assessing the knowledge and attitude of healthcare providers in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) regarding stem cells and their medical implications. The association between knowledge level and some epidemiological factors of the healthcare providers has also been considered. A self-administered questionnaire was developed by the researchers for the purposes of the study which was distributed among healthcare providers working in Thumbay Hospital Ajman and Thumbay Clinics across UAE of which 316 responses were collected. It was found that majority of the participants (59.8%) have an adequate knowledge of whom most were doctors in the age group of 41+ years. Interestingly, media was reported as the main source for knowledge on stem cells, while research work constituted the least knowledge source. Moreover, most of the participants (87.7%) especially doctors and dentists supported stem cells therapy. Furthermore, there was a clear link between knowledge level and positive attitude towards adopting stem cells therapy. Similarly, gender and years of experience were significantly associated with knowledge level. The study concluded with a recommendation to increase awareness on stem cells therapy and encourage healthcare providers to attend more conferences and seminars on this regard.

articleTitle: Development of Microwave Method for High-Precision Measurement of Water Percentage in Water-Oil Mixture
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The paper describes a new method for determining the percentage of water in a water-oil mixture, based on the use of a microwave communication channel to perform phase shift measurements with a simultaneous assessment of the degree of absorption of the microwave signal in the mixture under study. The calculated degree of absorption of the signal approximately determines the percentage of water in the mixture, which makes it possible to choose corresponding calibrated curve from the memory of solving unit and thereby unambiguously determine the percentage of water in the mixture. The phase difference of the signals is measured at low frequencies signals obtained after homodyne conversion of microwave signals, which makes it possible to obtain high measurement accuracy. Based on the proposed method the schematic diagram of the device has been developed and the theoretical possibilities of its operation have been considered. An experimental laboratory setup for measuring the volume percentage of water in oil and petroleum products has been developed and tested. The water content in water-oil mixtures with a mass concentration of water of 0.5, 10, 20 and 30% was studied. The average basic measurement error was ± 0.08, ± 0.35, ± 0.28 and ± 0.45%, respectively.

articleTitle: Impact of Financial Inclusion on Net Value Added by Economic Activity
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The study intends to analyze the impact of Financial Inclusion (FI) as viewed from the number of branches and access points of the Indian Post Payment Bank (IPPB) on the Net value added (NVA) by economic activities from banks and the insurance sector. The panel data model (PDM) is used to analyze the data of 19 states collected from 2019 to 2021. Findings indicate a positive impact of FI on NVA, suggesting an increase in the usage of IPPB as a tool of inclusion. This study has its own set of limitations. Certain states are not included in this study due to data unavailability, a shortcoming suggested to be resolved in the future by further studies. To the updated knowledge of authors, the inclusion of the insurance sector along with banks for consideration of NVA as an impact of FI is undertaken for the first time in this study.

articleTitle: Unveiling Public Perception of ChatGPT Through Twitter Data and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The study comprehensively analysed public sentiment towards ChatGPT, a language processing AI tool, using approximately 135,000 tweets from an initial dataset of 236,275 entries. After cleaning and pre-processing the data using basic NLP techniques, Machine Learning (ML) models—Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Decision Tree (DT), and Support Vector Machine (SVM)—were applied to classify the tweets into positive, negative, and neutral categories. The LSTM model demonstrated superior performance across all evaluation metrics—accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score—for all tweet categories. Word clouds generated for each category revealed that the most frequent words in positive tweets included ‘student,’ 'education,’ 'research,’ and ‘teacher,’ indicating a strong association of ChatGPT with educational and research contexts. Similarly, ‘AI,’ ‘student,’ 'research,’ ‘course,’ and ‘education’ dominated neutral and negative tweets, highlighting prevalent discussion topics. However, the study had limitations, including dependency on a single dataset, potential loss of contextual information during pre-processing, and a focus on English tweets only. Despite these limitations, the study provides valuable insights into the public’s perception of ChatGPT, underscoring its significant association with education and research and the effectiveness of the LSTM model in classifying tweets. The findings suggest that future research should incorporate diverse data sources and languages better to understand global sentiment towards ChatGPT and similar AI tools.

articleTitle: Segmentation of Railway Rails Using SAM
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Railways play a pivotal role in transportation infrastructure, but defects within them can lead to accidents and safety concerns. This article introduces an innovative approach for the automated segmentation of railway rails in images using the Segment Anything (SAM) model. SAM, a versatile image segmentation architecture, demonstrates the ability to segment objects without the need for extensive training data. In this study, the SAM model was applied to high-resolution railway images from the RailSem19 dataset, comprising 8,500 images. The results were remarkable, with an impressive, predicted Intersection over Union (IoU) score of 0.9760 for the left rail and 0.9595 for the right rail. This breakthrough offers a promising solution for enhancing railway safety and maintenance, showcasing SAM's potential to revolutionize image segmentation techniques in various applications.

articleTitle: Parallel Implementation of Random Forest using MPI
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Computer vision is a quickly rising field in machine learning. It has many use cases and implementations across various industries. Powerful classifiers can be trained to recognize visual patterns and detect people and objects. However, since these models use images as inputs, they often end up being trained with very complex architectures, with a high number of epochs and very large data sizes. This often results in very long training times, especially for weaker machines. This study investigated the use of parallel processing to speed up machine learning model training. Message-passing Interface (MPI) is used to parallelize the training of Random Forest, achieving speed-ups of up to 5 and an efficiency of up to 1.1. The study concludes that when dealing with big and complex data and building complex models, parallel processing can significantly reduce the training time of the model with minimal loss in accuracy.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Applicability of Different Portfolio Optimization Models across Three Emerging Markets under Different Market Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: In the realm of portfolio optimization, the Markowitz and Black-Litterman models play a significant role. This study closely examines their performance in three broad market indices; the Nifty-Fifty of India, the PSEi Composite of the Philippines, and the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI of Malaysia across diverse market conditions. The evaluation involves comparing portfolios, alongside market-cap-weighted portfolios, and using metrics like the Sharpe and Information ratios to gauge the effectiveness of the portfolios. Results revealed that MV performed better in economic crises, while B-L excelled in rapid market shifts and volatile conditions. B-L also outperformed during bullish trends, except in Malaysia. Both models offer insights, but adaptability varies. Investors should align models with market conditions, bridging theory and application.

articleTitle: Prevalidated Block for Improving Block Propagation in Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Blockchain is gaining worldwide acceptance in numerous fields. In contempt of its high-security feature, the current blockchain platform doesn’t provide a good transaction processing rate. Block propagation, the number of transactions processed per second, block transmission traffic, and block validation are the few performance parameters that affect its adoption. Transaction selection and ordering also play a very important role in block propagation. In this paper, we propose to split the block into two parts i.e. body of the block that contains the transactions and the header part of the block. The leader plays the role of selecting transactions from mempool and then orders them. The pre-matching algorithm is implemented to ensure that all of the nodes contain the similar body of the block which performs the pre-validation of the block being shared with all nodes. The block header is computed by the nodes selected by the leader. The final block header is shared with all of the nodes. This results in improving the block processing time, transmission traffic, and propagation time.

articleTitle: Classification of temperature break events in a reefer container using distance-based features
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Temperature breaks are a significant cause of quality deterioration in cold chain logistics. During transportation through reefer containers, the breaks occur primarily due to undesirable door opening and power failure. Detecting these incidents remotely from an edge node can mitigate quality loss by taking corrective actions. This paper presents a framework for classifying temperature break events from IoT data. The framework involves using a change detection algorithm to detect mean temperature shifts, followed by sub-sequence extraction for each event. Then, Dynamic Barycenter Averaging is used to create average sequences for each event class. The distances of a training sequence from each average sequence is used as a feature vector, which along with the event class creates a training dataset. A classifier is trained using these features for temperature break event identification. In ordered to create a labelled dataset, experiments are conducted in a reefer container, emulating various temperature events such as door opening, power failure, and corrective measures to reach the desired temperature. A comparative study is carried out with several distance-based methods and six classifiers. The results demonstrate that a accuracy of 98.4% is achieved. Finally, the trained classifier can be easily implemented on an edge node placed within a refrigerated container for real-time event alerting during transportation.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition using Eye Movements: A review
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Human activity recognition represents a prominent and formidable challenge within the domain of computer vision. This problem holds substantial relevance across various domains, encompassing robotics, gaming, therapeutic interventions, human-robot interaction, athletic performance analysis, healthcare monitoring, and video surveillance. Due to the complicated human pose variations and group interactions, human activity recognition is difficult. Some of these inherent difficulties could be solved using sensors with several modalities. An RGB-D camera, thermal sensors, infrared sensors etc. might all be examples of such sensors. Due to intrusive nature of these sensing modalities it may cause user inconvenience which limits its utility to a broader audience. To overcome this, in this work, we explore eye movement analysis for sensing activity recognition. Eye movement analysis has become a promising method for identifying human activities across a variety of fields. This paper provides a review of techniques and applications for eye movement analysis in human activity recognition. The study examines the possibility of detecting human activity using a low-cost, camera based eye gaze tracking device and opens up discussion on the wider applicability of eye movements based activity recognition that are difficult, or even impossible, to detect using common sensing modalities.

articleTitle: Inverse Power Log-Toppleone distribution and its competitors for estimating the exchange rate datasets
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This study developed an alternative distribution to any generalized Weibull, Gamma and several well-known distributions in the literature called Inverse Power Log-Toppleone distribution for estimating the exchange rate datasets. The simplest form and quantile function were obtained while the maximum likelihood approach applied for estimating the parameters. In addition, two datasets for exchange rate were analyzed and check for the best fitted model. Based on the results available for the two datasets the proposed model outperformed its competitors for estimating the datasets based on measure criteria.

articleTitle: Data Center Lab Using VxLAN Data Plane and BGP-EVPN Control Plane
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Virtual Extensible Local Area Network is an overlay technology that allows smart encapsulation of layer two through layer three. It provides the extension of Virtual Local Area Network domains, allowing the original addressing of virtual hosts through the data centers and cloud computing networks. Furthermore, The traditional three-layer model data center architecture can be abandoned with a more efficient topology, known as Spine and Leaf. The Spine and Leaf topology offers low latency and high bandwidth, which are crucial for high-performance computing and cloud environments. Moreover, by incorporating VXLAN technology with the Spine and Leaf architecture, it will provide an effective network topology, which considers the demands of modern data center networks. This paper introduces the VxLAN Multiprotocol Border Gateway Protocol, Ethernet Virtual Private Network (MP-BGP EVPN), and provides a practical implementation using the Free Range Router with docker containers in a GNS3 environment.

articleTitle: Predicting Electricity Consumption Using Load Profiling Clustering Method
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: It became crucial to analyze the energy consumption trends from smart meter data to identify potential saving opportunities by the electricity suppliers and authorities since energy consumption is considered one of the essential topics of energy systems which gained high attention after the energy crisis in 1970’s. Despite that smart meter data analytics is relatively recent field, the progress in high performance computing makes it possible to efficiently and effectively extracting more beneficial knowledge and patterns from collected massive data within the smart grid. This research aims at providing a model for predicting load profiling while considering the temporal feature of the smart meter data by deploying a deep clustering algorithm embedded with an autoencoder and compare it with the dynamic autoencoder which can improve the prediction quality while applying dimensionality reduction and evaluate these models based on the performance using the silhouette score. The dynamic autoencoder outperformed the deep embedded clustering (DEC) and improved deep embedded clustering (IDEC) models and achieved a silhouette score of 0.9931 compared to DEC of 0.6128 and IDEC of 0.8829. This shows that positioning a dynamic autoencoder embedded with deep clustering model has worked effectively against the problem of feature drift and feature randomness.

articleTitle: User Centered Agile Software Development: Emerging Themes and Future Trends
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Despite having several advantages, agile methodology and its variants tend to hamper the development of innovative solutions as end-user needs are not considered. The integration of Agile to User Centered Design is therefore a topic of great interest for both academicians and industry professionals as it enables organizations to benefit from the advantages of agile methods while working on its drawbacks. The analytical tools ScientoPy, VOSviewer and bibliometrix were used to understand the co-relationships between 542 articles obtained from the Scopus database using the scientometric technique. Following a review which spans from the conception of agile in 2001 to the present date, generic concepts such as usability, humans, and usability evaluation and specific terms such as commerce, aged, adult and outcome assessment surfaced as the main keywords. Furthermore, most of the concepts referred to in 2002-2012 have emerged as software design in the last 10 years. Usability, agile methods, and usability evaluation were identified as the trendiest topics even though these three are below 20% with the slightest percentage of documents published in the last years 2021-2022. The trend analysis shows the decline of usability, agile methods, and usability evaluation and the emergence of systematic literature review, UX, MHealth and mobile apps.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Computational Performance of Different Quantum Circuits on Different IBMQ Backends: Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Quantum computers are difficult to reach by researchers because of the difficulty in manufacturing technologies and the need to provide ideal working conditions. As a solution, IBM Quantum (IBMQ) systems developed by IBM are accessed via the cloud. Although there are high qubit quantum backends currently offered for a fee, 5 and 7 qubit backends are publicly free. In this study, publicly free quantum backends in the IBM quantum experience environment are discussed. The study includes a comparative explanation of the factors affecting the performance of quantum computers. Quantum circuits were created in the IBM Composer environment and then run on the appropriate backend. Quantum circuits of 4mod5, which finds whether a 4-bit number is divisible by 5, 1-bitadder that performs 1-bit addition with the carry bit, and gray code, which finds the gray code equivalent of the binary number, were created. The created circuits were run on 8 different IBMQ backends and the results were analyzed. As a result of the analysis, it has been shown that while the simplicity of the gates used increases the performance rates, there may be different backends that operate each quantum circuit more accurately. It is hoped that the study will be a guide for researchers working on applied quantum computing.

articleTitle: A New Approach to in Ensemble Method for Deepfake Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: With the great development of technology and deep learning gaining competence in many areas, recently forgery of images has started to pose great threats and become the main topic of most technology companies. But here, with the ongoing race between good and evil, new approaches have emerged in fraud detection. Since this technological development is bilateral, fraud detection is constantly trying to be developed and trying to catch fraud. In this regard, various approaches have emerged by many different companies and people to contribute to society. In the method we have proposed to contribute to these detection processes and to detect forgery, feature extraction is provided on images using the D-CNN model, and with these features, SVM, Estimation is done on features with Random Forest and Logistic Regression. Finally, using the Ensemble method, an estimation process is performed by taking all the estimates together with the sampling on the images. Thanks to this proposed method, the determinations made are supported in a layered way and precision is ensured at the accuracy rate.

articleTitle: Detecting the Past: Advancements in Comic Panel Detection for Cultural Heritage Preservation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The preservation and restoration of historical murals is a crucial task in the field of cultural heritage preservation. In this study, we explored the use of comic panel detection technology for the preservation of historical murals. Specifically, we applied the faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (R-CNN) algorithm, a state-of-the-art object detection algorithm, for the detection and segmentation of individual panels in historical murals. We developed a dataset of high-resolution photographs of historical murals and evaluated the performance of the algorithm using several metrics, including precision, recall, F1 score, and mean average precision (mAP). The algorithm achieved high precision, recall, and F1 score values across all five folds, with an average mAP value of 0.86. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the comic panel detection algorithm in accurately detecting and segmenting individual panels in historical murals. Additionally, we conducted a case study on a partially damaged historical mural, where the panel segmentation provided valuable information for the restoration process. The restoration process successfully restored the damaged areas of the mural while preserving the original composition and color scheme. Overall, this study highlights the potential of comic panel detection technology in the field of cultural heritage preservation and underscores the importance of technology in supporting these efforts.

articleTitle: Smart Health Monitoring Framework for the Prevention of Infectious Diseases
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: In the recent past, COVID-19 has emerged as one of the major health emergencies throughout the world which has given stimulus to the research to propose smart health monitoring systems for the prevention of contagious diseases. The proposed research is an effort towards this direction which offers a framework for smart health monitoring systems, for the prevention of contagious diseases. The system includes an adhesive element configured to the skin of humans, which includes a set of sensors configured to discover numerous fitness parameters of the person and a configured processing unit. The vital parameters-based health data collected from the proposed systems can be used to examine whether the received values are within the predefined desired ranges. A warning unit is configured in the processing unit that is activated upon receiving the set of warning alerts from the processing unit. Further, the system’s warning unit provides alerts to take precautions to save ourselves from the transmission of infectious diseases. Additionally, this paper results in a strong and efficient solution for an accurate infectious disease monitoring system.

articleTitle: Classification of Multi-Label Electrocardiograms Utilizing the EfficientNet CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Using electrocardiogram (ECG) signal images, the status of Covid-19, Abnormal heartbeat, Myocardial infarction, Myocardial Infarction History and Normal findings can be detected. Disease detections made with traditional methods by specialist doctors in the field can lead to mistreatment due to human error. The successes obtained from the classification studies using ECG images in the literature do not have an acceptable success rate yet. The aim of this study is to propose a new approach with high success rate for the detection of diseases using ECG images and to analyze detailed test results. A publicly available dataset containing 5-class ECG images was used in this study. Training and testing processes were carried out using the EfficientNetB0 convolutional neural network architecture. Afterwards, the results were analyzed in detail, graphs were drawn and the results were compared with other studies in the literature. The proposed multi-class classification architecture offers 99.13% accuracy. With the success achieved, it was superior to other studies in the literature. This study will contribute to the rapid and reliable detection of 5 different findings that can be detected from ECG images and to more accurate treatment of patients.

articleTitle: Random Walker based Automated Phase Discrimination and Morphological Insights in Ultra-High Carbon Steel
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Image analysis is an important process required for characterization in different engineering domains. This work presents a novel image processing methodology to segment phases and quantify grain morphology in ultra-high carbon steel (UHCS) micrographs. Unlike conventional global thresholding methods, an interactive random walker technique which leverages user-defined markers for localized phase discrimination was deployed. Adaptive histogram equalization enhances contrast to identify seed markers representing distinct phases. The random walker algorithm propagates labels from these seeds by minimizing an edge-weighted cost function. This interactive approach provides precise phase boundaries despite variability in grain morphology. The segmented output enables statistical grain size, shape, and orientation quantification. The study demonstrates the UHCS micrograph data for an input grayscale image, and the mean area, mean intensity, and mean orientation of all the grains are computed to be 716.667 px<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 129.449, and -53.648, respectively. By combining accessible preprocessing, interactive localization, and rigorous postprocessing, our pipeline automates the characterization of microstructural features from image customizable nature of this physics-based machine learning technique makes it widely applicable for robust characterization of varied material microstructures from images.

articleTitle: Federated Learning for Temperature Break Identification in a Reefer Container from IoT Data
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Perishable items transported through cold chain logistics(CCL) are susceptible to quality deterioration due to temperature breaks. The reefer container, which maintains the desired temperature during transit, can experience breaks due to door openings and power failures. An intelligent IoT device installed in the reefer container can generate real-time alerts for nearby operators to take corrective measures. Supervised machine learning models can identify the causes of the temperature breaks, but they require a large amount of high-quality labeled data for training. To generate labeled data for different temperature events, we conducted an experiment. The experimental data includes door openings, power failures, and corrective measures, such as the temperature settling to the set point. In CCL, temperature breaks are infrequent, leading to a scarcity of data that hampers training due to a limited sample size. To overcome this challenge, we propose a federated learning approach aimed at developing a generalized global model. In this approach, the edge device trains a local model with its dataset, and the local parameters generated from different containers are aggregated on the server to create a global model. The global model is then sent back to the edge device to update its local model. This approach avoids the need for communicating data, reducing bandwidth, biases, computation, and latency. The study shows that using the federated learning architecture the models accuracy is similar to those trained with the complete dataset for temperature break identification.

articleTitle: A Culture-Aware Deep Architecture for Emotional State Detection from Facial Expressions
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Emotion detection is one of the widely explored fields and finds application in almost every domain. However, culture impacts the emotional regulation of a person. Thus, cultural information needs to be incorporated while designing systems for automatic detection of emotions. This study presents a culture- aware deep-learning based methodology for detection of emotions from facial expressions. Facial expressions of models belonging to Japan, North Europe and Mediterranean regions were analysed using a Multi-Layer Perceptron based deep network, in which individual layers are actually independent models trained on data of a particular region. The proposed culture-aware architecture got an accuracy of 87.9% and outperformed the individual submodels by a great margin.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Production Planning and Supply Chain Management: A Brief Review
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Nowadays, the industry is constantly evolving. Digital transformation has become an enormously important catalyst, profoundly reshaping companies’ operations management, particularly in production planning and supply chain management. Underlined by the advent of Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0, it requires a strategic orchestration of technologies, including the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), Big Data (BD), Digital Manufacturing (DM), and Artificial Intelligence (AI), among others. In this sense, the role of data-based methodologies is crucial since they facilitate precision and efficiency within the processes. Decision support tools that leverage data-driven technologies empower industries to tackle complex challenges, such as manufacturing a wide range of products within tight lead times, recognizing forecast patterns, specific predictive maintenance activities, and optimizing production planning and supply chain management. In this context, this work aims to recognize and characterize the primary research in data-driven production planning and supply chain management that has taken place in recent years. The proposed methodology adopts a Systematic Literature Review (SLR). Preliminary findings indicate a sustained growth in research interest beginning in 2017, with Germany, the United States, and China emerging as leaders. International collaborations underscore the global nature of this field of research while demonstrating a relative regional centrality and a vacancy in Latin America. Besides, the most predominant emerging topics are recognized. The discussions of this research refer to the evolution of the scientific activity of these disciplines in the regional context and provide an overview of the evolution of research on data-driven production planning and supply chain management.

articleTitle: Car Logo Recognition using YOLOv8 and Microsoft Azure Custom Vision
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This research is conducted with its main objective to develop an accurate and faster model that can identify brands from logos captured through car images used by Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah (UMPSA) staff. The software used for this case study is You Only Look Once (YOLO) version 8 and Microsoft Azure's Custom Vision. Each software was compared and results from the analysis showed that YOLOv8 is renowned for its speed and efficiency and is capable of real-time object detection, which makes it ideal for applications where speed is critical. However, this approach might occasionally compromise accuracy, especially for smaller objects or objects that are close together. Microsoft Azure Custom Vision, on the other hand, may not be as fast as YOLOv8, but it generally delivers high accuracy, especially if adequately trained with a diverse set of tagged images. To conclude, the choice between YOLOv8 and Microsoft Azure Custom Vision depends on the specific requirements of the project, technical expertise, and resources.

articleTitle: IoT Gateway Bulk Driven Quasi Floating PLL Logic In 5G Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Modern radio communication equipment makes significant use of Phase Locked Loop (PLL) frequency synthesizers. Users can choose from a set of frequencies to generate a set of frequencies based on one reference. We use conventional PLLs using complementary metal oxide semiconductors (CMOS) and BD MOS transistors configured in a pass transistor mode to design a PLL that reaches 140 MHz. Circuits have been simulated based on SPICE at a transistor level of 0.18um. A reference signal of 20kHz is used for the generation of a clock at 140MHz. Frequency divider circuits utilize BD QFG Pass transistor logic PLLs as principles. To achieve an almost 10GHz frequency, the frequency divider is utilized.

articleTitle: Python: An Automation Tool for Unlocking Innovation and Efficiency in the AEC Sector
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Python offers a lot of potential as an automation tool for the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry, with opportunities to enhance decision-making, accelerate innovation, and simplify operations. The AEC industry challenges issues with efficiency, innovation, and sustainable development in the current data-driven world. Automation has proven a potent cure, revolutionizing many aspects of business. Python provides potential to enhance operational efficiency by minimizing AEC operations, enhancing decision-making, and exploiting its extensive libraries and flexibility. This research examines the adoption of automation technologies in the AEC industry, including computer-aided design (CAD), building information modelling (BIM), robotics, and machine learning, through a review of the literature, guidelines, and criteria that are assessed according to their effect. It exposes the deficiencies and problems, such as the lack of software system compatibility. Due to its versatility, considerable community support, and potential for connection with existing software systems, Python presents as a feasible automation solution. The findings reinforce the significance of continuing research and application in this sector by demonstrating the benefits of Python automation in encouraging collaboration, innovation, and a data-driven future for the AEC industry.

articleTitle: Overcoming the Challenges of Implementing Cloud Computing in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Education is one of the essential pillars of a country's social and economic growth. Despite the birth of the global pandemic in recent years, educational institutions must continue to innovate in providing the necessary means for faculties and students to perform academic tasks with limited resources. Now, everyone has become more technologically connected, in part, due to the Internet. Education systems all over the globe are slowly incorporating cloud applications into their learning environment because of the various benefits that it has to offer. Depending on the institution’s needs, various cloud-based products are accessible by service providers to ensure the education system is running smoothly. This paper provides an overview of the benefits of cloud computing and outlines its main features, service, and deployment models for higher education, such as its ability to improve collaboration, reduce costs, and increase scalability. The paper also discusses the challenges that institutions face in implementing cloud computing, such as security and data privacy concerns. Finally, the paper provides recommendations for institutions that are considering implementing cloud computing. These recommendations include conducting a needs assessment, selecting the right cloud provider, and developing a security plan.

articleTitle: Leveraging AI Techniques for Enhanced Software Defect Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: In software engineering (SE), software defect prediction (SDP) plays a pivotal role in enhancing software quality by detecting defects during development. However, the challenge of imbalanced datasets significantly impacts the efficiency of defect prediction models. This study leverages Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques to overcome these challenges and improve defect prediction. We explore ensemble methods, resampling with cost-sensitive learning, and anomaly detection via Transfer Learning (TL). Experiments on NASA MDP’s PC2 and AEEEM’s JDT datasets demonstrate our strategies' effectiveness, particularly in managing imbalanced data. Notable outcomes include a 95% accuracy, 97% precision, 98% recall, and an F1-score of 97% for the ensemble model on the PC2 dataset and similarly with the JDT dataset. These AI-driven techniques represent a substantial advancement in SDP. Furthermore, our One-Class Support Vector Machine (SVM) anomaly detection identifies 115 anomalies in the PC2 dataset, with similar results in the JDT dataset. TL broadens predictive capabilities, providing insights from a wider context. These outcomes underscore the significant impact of AI-driven techniques in navigating the complexities of SDP and advancing defect prediction models.

articleTitle: A Security Driven Energy Efficient Workflow Allocation Algorithm under Deadline Constraints for Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Cloud computing has risen as a prevalent approach for providing diverse internet-based services to users. Workflow allocation in cloud environments is a critical task that involves the efficient allocation of tasks to appropriate resources. The energy consumption and security aspects of workflow allocation are important considerations that impact the overall performance and reliability of cloud-based systems. This paper proposes a novel algorithm, named the Security-Driven Energy-Efficient Workflow Allocation Algorithm (SEWA), which addresses these challenges by considering energy efficiency, and security to satisfy the deadline and precedence constraints of the task. The SEWA algorithm intelligently allocates workflow tasks to cloud resources while minimizing energy consumption, ensuring security requirements, and meeting deadlines. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of the SEWA algorithm in achieving significant energy savings, enhancing security, and meeting workflow deadlines. The experiments are conducted using realistic workflows such as CyberShake, Montage, and LIGO and cloud infrastructure models. The performance metrics include risk probability and energy consumption.

articleTitle: A Predictive Approach to Mobile-only Banking Adoption in Bahrain: Evidence from Decision Trees
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Mobile-only banking is revolutionizing all over the world and is expanding in Bahrain due to its numerous benefits. It provides greater convenience, availability, reduced transactional costs, and easier customer access to financial information. The lack of customers’ adoption of mobile-only banking services is considered the main challenge service providers are facing. This can lead to huge financial losses and failures if not addressed in the correct way. Thus, it is vital for bank management to identify customer’s adoption patterns and the most influential factors affecting the adoption to facilitate the acceptance and usage of this service. Based on the results, strategies need to be formulated to increase the adoption rates and profitability. In this paper, J48 decision tree algorithm was used in WEKA to build a predictive model in order to classify users into adopters and non-adopters, predict customer adoption in case of new or unseen customers, and identify the most important attributes affecting the adoption of mobile-only banking in Bahrain. The proposed model showed a satisfactory accuracy rate.

articleTitle: Explainable AI-Driven Machine Learning Approach for Prediction of Acoustic-Based Fire Extinction
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Acoustic fire-extinguishing system is an alternative system for the safe handling and control of fire accidents by extinguishing different classes of fires. It is necessary to accurately identify and predict the extinction and non-extinction states of the flames based on certain characteristic features. It is also important to identify the most important features governing the classification of the states of the flame. Both of these can be achieved by the combination of deep learning techniques and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). In this study, models like artificial neural networks (ANN) and convolution neural networks (CNN) were deployed on an experimental dataset to classify the extinction states of the flame based on features, namely, flame sizes, fuel type, airflow, decibel, frequencies, and distance range. On the implementation of ANN, 95% and 92% accuracy were obtained, while 97% and 98% accuracy were obtained on a CNN model, for the liquid and LPG fuels respectively. The application of XAI in this study indicates that distance range has the maximum impact among all features of the model.

articleTitle: The Carbon Footprint of Net Zero Buildings: A Critical Review
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The idea of "net zero" buildings has received a lot of interest as a potential solution to reduce carbon emissions in the construction industry. However, real-world consequences frequently fall short of idealistic expectations. This research critically examines the current paradigm on net zero buildings, highlighting the hidden carbon emissions within these ostensibly sustainable constructions. It highlights gaps in present practices, discusses barriers to obtain net-zero status, and thoroughly studies the elements contributing to these buildings' carbon emissions. The study proposes a comprehensive strategy that includes both operational and embedded carbon emissions and methods for reducing emissions throughout the building's life cycle. Additionally, the study analyses the consequences and suggestions for legislators, developers, and industry stakeholders to accelerate the adoption of net zero building practices. The analysis considers that by following these principles and adopting a comprehensive approach, net zero buildings may realise their objective of lowering carbon emissions and supporting a profitable, low-carbon-built environment.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology in Construction Industry: Current State and Future Trends through Bibliometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Blockchain technology has gained significant attention in the construction industry due to its potential to address critical challenges such as fragmentation, inefficiency, and a lack of stakeholder trust. Due to the growing research in this area, it has become essential to understand the evolving landscape comprehensively and identify the current state of research and future directions in the field of blockchain technology in construction. This paper aims to achieve this by conducting a bibliometrics analysis to map blockchain’s trends and research landscape in construction.
