The bibliometric analysis of scholarly articles and conference papers published in the Scopus database was used to identify the yearly trend of publications, influential authors, leading countries, prominent research institutions, and top journals in this field. Additionally, co-occurrence keywords were analyzed to explore the key themes and identify emerging trends and future research directions in blockchain-based construction. This study provides valuable insights for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers interested in understanding the current state and future prospects of blockchain technology in the construction industry. It also serves as a primary reference source for further studies in this area.

articleTitle: Exploring the Role of Mathematical Modelling in Automatic Scene Generation amidst Rapid Technological Advances
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: There is a need for an algorithm that can analyse the input language and build computational scenario models so that images, movie clips, and other digital artefacts may be related and the video can be composed on the fly in order to generate videos automatically from text clues. In this paper, therefore, a novel text scripting analytics engine for scene production that would aid in the creation of automatic films and film clips has been mathematically proposed. The Text Scripting Analytical Model (TSAM) is a configurable and easy to implement algorithm that uses multiple techniques to parse the input, identify the entities, and construct a scene into an automatic visual representation. In terms of performance expectations, the algorithm is anticipated to exhibit small execution times in milliseconds, albeit with a relatively high level of complexity.

articleTitle: Telecommunications Fraud Machine Learning-based Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Telecommunications fraud has been continuously causing severe problems to businesses resulting in huge financial damage, complete closure, or even a hard collapse. Despite the new approaches and fraud prevention tools, fraudsters are still finding ways out to trick their victims to achieve their target: avoid paying bills or acquire money illegally. With the proliferation of new technologies, numerous vulnerabilities are divulged for fraudsters who perform illegal activities. Thus, the need for effective fraud detection systems and strategies is essential. The aim of this survey paper is to investigate the types of telecommunications fraud, as well as current fraud detection techniques while discussing the performance of the different approaches to overcome such challenges. We review the state of the art, while presenting also our Machine-Learning based approaches in evaluating different models to detect international revenue share fraud before concluding with our recommendations and perspectives.

articleTitle: A Bibliometric Analysis on the Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Petroleum Engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) continues to make transformative strides across various sectors, its applications in Petroleum Engineering have garnered increasing attention for tasks such as reservoir management, drilling optimization, and predictive maintenance. However, a comprehensive understanding of the existing body of research at the intersection of AI and Petroleum Engineering remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis aimed at identifying and mapping the current status of AI and petroleum engineering research from 2014 to August 2023, while also highlighting its possible future paths. A total of 474 documents were sourced from Scopus database and analyzed using state-of-the-art bibliometric tools using "VOSviewer". The analysis includes most active countries, prolific journals, keyword co-occurrence, and emerging research areas associated with the AI and petroleum engineering. The analysis highlights the progression of research interest over time and identifies the pivotal topics that have shaped discussions within the field. Furthermore, this study provides insights into potential future directions of the AI and petroleum engineering, enabling researchers, practitioners, and stakeholders to anticipate and contribute to the ongoing development of the energy sector. Through this bibliometric exploration, the paper not only offers a consolidated overview of existing knowledge but also serves as valuable insights for those seeking to navigate the this multidisciplinary research area.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study For Predicting House Price Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This study presents the development and comparison of four machine learning approaches, namely, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Linear Regression and k-Nearest Neighbours (k-NN), to perform house prices prediction based employing the Boston Housing Dataset. The approaches performance was evaluated using root mean square error as well as R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, with the aim of identifying the model that best predicts housing prices. The dataset was thoroughly analyzed for features, correlations, multicollinearity, and overfitting. Results indicate that the RF model outperformed the other models in predicting house prices, as it has ability to address non-linearity and complex interactions among variables and reduce the impact of outliers. The DT model also performed well but may have been more prone to overfitting. LR, on the other hand, may have been limited by its assumptions of linearity and independence among variables.

articleTitle: Traffic Signal Violation Detection Through Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This research offers an advanced computer vision-based traffic signal violation detection. The suggested technology seeks to instantly detect and report traffic signal violations such as running red lights. The approach suggested in this research can precisely and effectively detect infractions by combining advanced computer vision algorithms with deep learning approaches. By improving overall traffic safety, the introduction of this approach is expected to have a substantial positive influence on people's ease. Law enforcement authorities are better able to respond quickly to risky driving practices, lowering the risk of accidents and enhancing traffic management, as a result of automated traffic infraction detection and reporting. The proposed solution’s real-time capabilities will make it less likely for drivers to disobey the law, encouraging better driving practices and reducing the likelihood of accidents.

articleTitle: Sort-O-Matic: An efficient Waste Segregation System for Sustainable Waste Management
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Waste segregation is one of the most critical processes that need to be focused on especially these days when production has increased in response to the increase in the number of consumers. Increased production has led to an increase in waste generation as well. Waste management starts with waste segregation. Segregation of waste is the principal step in the proper management of waste. More time and manpower are required to segregate the waste using traditional methods. Also, traditional methods pose a risk to human health as waste segregation involves dealing with a lot of toxic substances. Analyzing and grouping of waste into different categories by using different sensors can increase waste processing efficiency. In this study, an autonomous system of waste segregation using sensors has designed. For the classification of wastes into different categories A88 metal proximity sensor, a customized moisture detection sensor, an IR sensor, and an Ultrasonic sensor have been used. The findings from the system ensured that proposed system efficiently segregate the waste material as per their properties. Furthermore, it helps the users to reuse and recycle the waste material to make the goods.

articleTitle: Simulation of DDoS Attack in Software Defined Networking
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This paper aims to propose an approach to detecting attacks against the controller of software-defined networking (SDN) that use distributed denial (problems) of service (DDoS). As SDN is a popular model for managing and controlling network traffic, it has become a prime target for attackers seeking to disrupt the network. The central SDN controller serves as the network's brain in the control plane. The goal of this separation is to make resources more manageable, secure, and controllable. But still these networks are becoming target of lethal threats such as DDoS attacks and still it is an open issue to detect and mitigate such attacks. In this paper, we use methods to identify DDoS attacks on SDN controller i.e., ODL (OpenDaylight). These methods are based on network traffic analysis. Specifically, especially here we utilize Ubuntu, Mininet, and Wireshark to make, host, and detect attacks on SDN controller. To evaluate the effectiveness of our approach, we conducted experiments using a simulated SDN network environment and DDoS attack is transmission control protocol synchronization (TCP SYN). The findings show that our method can effectively and efficiently identify DDoS attacks with low erroneous rates, thus offering a potential option for increasing the safeguards of SDN networks.

articleTitle: Digital Twins: Facilitating Digital Transformation From and Beyond BIM in Construction
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Industry 4.0 technologies are revolutionizing conventional practices across various sectors and stand at the forefront of digital transformation within these industries. Building Information Modeling (BIM) technology has modernized the construction sector, an industry known for low innovation but high GDP contribution, over the last few years. The adoption of Digital Twins (DT) technology is now enriching BIM, particularly in addressing the dynamic aspects of construction processes. This empowers the utilization of real-time data for more resilient data-driven practices, resulting in heightened productivity and accelerated progress in digital transformation. A systematic review is imperative as the construction industry needs to keep up with the fast-paced digital economy. Therefore, this paper aims to investigate the status of digital transformation by using the PRISMA methodology for systematic review. The Scopus database was referred to using specific keywords, and 52 documents were obtained and filtered to 15 final records. Literature analysis about DT-driven digitalization in construction provides insights into the transitional stages and pillars guiding the digital transformation phenomenon. This study will provide valuable insights into the future DT trends in the sector and enable the realization of digitalization in the construction industry.

articleTitle: Safeguarding Business Intelligence in Industrial IoT Using Blockchain-Enhanced Security
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: In Industry 4.0, the rapid development of ICT has transformed various industries, including the Internet of Things and big data analytics, which introduces the concept of IIoT (Industrial Internet of Things). IIoT depends on data connectivity infrastructures, analytics, humans, and intelligent assets that store and transmit data to work. The IIoT network's large number of components also increases the possibility of security issues. The integration of Business Intelligence (BI) in Industrial Internet of Things (IoT) systems has exposed critical data to security threats. Existing security measures are inadequate, necessitating research into more robust solutions. This research aims to enhance the security of BI in Industrial IoT by leveraging blockchain technology. The objective is to design and implement a blockchain-based security framework to safeguard sensitive industrial data. The study presents a novel blockchain-enhanced security system for Industrial IoT, effectively safeguarding BI data. The evaluation demonstrates improved data integrity, confidentiality, and traceability, highlighting the potential of blockchain as a robust security solution in industrial settings. This paper also shows that integrating IIoT, Blockchain, and business intelligence can improve a firm's performance, which needs various types of data collection from different sources. Blockchain's essential qualities that greatly impact IIoT's security flaws are decentralization, immutability, and tamper-proof. This is why IIoT is a field in which blockchain technology is very important. The implications are going to be beneficial for smart industries in order to develop next-generation secure IIoT.

articleTitle: Driver Drowsiness Detection Using Computer Vision and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: It is alarming that car crashes resulting in damage to automobiles, injuries to passengers, and loss of lives occur daily. The incidence of road crashes is rapidly increasing worldwide and has drawn many road safety commissions and concerned individuals to discuss ways to drastically reduce this menacing situation. The introduction of artificial intelligence and technological advancement has prompted government agencies and state commissions to call upon universities and research institutions to develop methods to curb the rise of automobile crashes. These crashes can be attributed to various factors, including drunk driving and, most notably, drowsiness, which affects a wide range of individuals. Drowsiness detection can be categorized into three main techniques; behavioral-based, vehicular-based, and physiological-based. In this research, the behavioral-based approach was studied, with significant consideration being the cost of implementation, execution time, and accuracy. Three machine learning (ML) classifiers were considered: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naïve Bayes (NB), and Random Forest (RF). A dataset of 1448 images was used for training and testing these classifiers: 70% for training and 30% for testing. Random Forest classifier gave the best accuracy of (92.41) compared to SVM (90.34) and Naïve Bayes (69.43).

articleTitle: Land cover mapping using Landsat 8 data and supervised learning classifiers in Casablanca region, Morocco
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This study focuses on assessing the effectiveness of various supervised algorithms in classifying Landsat satellite images over the region of Casablanca, Morocco. The region's rapid urbanization and land cover changes make it an ideal case study for evaluating the performance of algorithms in capturing diverse land cover types. The methodology involves data collection in the platform Google Earth Engine (GEE), preprocessing steps, supervised algorithms, and metrics of assessment. The findings provide valuable insights for decision-making processes and sustainable urban development in the region. Overall, this study contributes to the understanding of the most suitable algorithm for Landsat satellite image classification in Casablanca and lays the groundwork for future advancements in remote sensing applications. This paper presents an experimental study of three supervised machine-learning algorithms. These are Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Minimum Distance (MD). The objective is to classify the different zones such as water, built-up, cropped, barren, and forest areas within the city of Casablanca. The classification results are evaluated using various accuracy indicators, including Overall Accuracy (OA), Kappa Coefficient, User Accuracy (UA), and Producer Accuracy (PA). The Random Forest (RF) algorithm recorded the best accuracy, reaching 95.42%. In contrast, the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm performed the worst, with an accuracy of just 83%.

articleTitle: Analyzing the performance of supervised and unsupervised learning for satellite image classification: A case study of Casablanca
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Satellite image classification plays a crucial role in various applications such as urban planning, environmental monitoring, and land use analysis. In this study, we present a comparative analysis of different supervised and unsupervised learning methods for satellite image classification, focusing on a case study in Casablanca using Landsat 8 imagery. The aim of this research is to identify the most effective machine-learning approach for accurately classifying land cover in an urban environment. The study begins with a comprehensive review of satellite image classification techniques and machine learning methods commonly used in this field. We explore the strengths and limitations of each method used, such as Random Forest, Cart and Support Vector Machines (SVMs), etc. Using Landsat imagery data from Casablanca, we pre-process the data, extract relevant features, and partition them into training and test sets. Through a series of experiments, we evaluate the performance of each machine learning method in terms of accuracy, and Kappa coefficient. Our results highlight the varying abilities of these methods to accurately classify different land-use categories in an urban context. We discuss the factors that influence their performance, including data characteristics, feature selection, and model complexity.

articleTitle: The Effect of Green Banking, Green Image, And Bank Trust on Bank Loyalty
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Green Banking is a broad word that refers to bank operations and policies that are sustainable in economic, environmental, and social dimensions. This refers to specific banking actions and practices that assist in reducing total external carbon emissions as well as internal carbon footprint. One example is the growing trend of cashless payments using mobile app services. This study investigates the effects of green banking, green image, and bank trust on bank loyalty. This is an explanatory study that employs a quantitative approach and survey methodology. With a total of 183 respondents, the sampling strategy employed was simple random sampling. This study employed the Structural Equation Modeling analysis approach with the SmartPLS 3.0 analysis tool. A statistical method used to analyze the complex relationships between variables in an integrated model. Green banking, green image, and bank trust were found to have a substantial impact on bank loyalty. This research suggested factors to be improved, such as green banking, green image, and bank trust to continue adapting to customer needs.

articleTitle: Predictive Model for Early Detection of Cardiovascular, Renal and Neurodegenerative Disorder Using Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This investigation is concerned with the difficulties of quickly diagnosing diseases while working with various disease-specific datasets. It addresses these issues in the context of cardiovascular illnesses, neurological problems, and severe renal ailments by applying approaches like dimensionality reduction, particularly using Principal Component Analysis (PCA). The study investigates how several machine learning methods, such as Random Forest, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K Nearest Neighbours (KNN), and Logistic Regression, perform when used after PCA. The study contrasts the efficacy of models with and without PCA to show the advantages of dimensionality reduction techniques. Notably, KNN predicts Chronic Kidney Disease with a flawless 100% accuracy whereas Logistic Regression predicts Cardiovascular Disease with an 85% accuracy. Additionally, when evaluated on the Alzheimer's Neuroimaging Initiatives (ADNI) cohort, the suggested machine learning algorithms demonstrate a remarkable 97.82% accuracy. This demonstrates the efficiency of Logistic Regression in predicting cardiac illness and backs up the applicability of KNN for identifying kidney-related problems.

articleTitle: Circular Economy and Industry 4.0: A Review of Their Role in Advancing Sustainable Development Goals
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) provide a comprehensive framework to address society’s most pressing challenges and promote Sustainability. Dual Emerging Paradigms, Circular Economy (CE) and Industry 4.0 (I-4.0) have gained significant attention for their potential to drive systemic change and support SDG achievement. A systematic literature review explores the correlation between CE practices and I-4.0 technologies in advancing the SDGs. Using a scientific mapping approach, the study employs bibliographic coupling analysis, including source and country analysis and keyword co-occurrence analysis. VOS viewer software analyses 111 articles published from 2018 to July 2023 to understand how the integration of CE and I-4.0 contributes to the SDGs. Results directly impact SDGs 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, and 13, addressing specific targets within these goals. The CE-I-4.0 nexus connects innovative technologies with circular business models, offering a promising avenue for SDG progress. Future research can focus on quantifying these impacts and exploring more case studies. This systematic review is valuable for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers, offering insights into how CE and I-4.0 can contribute to SDG attainment. The study’s scope is limited to English articles in the Scopus database.

articleTitle: A Cardinality-Constrained Portfolio Selection Model Using Golden Eagle Optimizer in Stock Markets
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This electronic document is a "live" template and Abstract—In the realm of capital markets, it is imperative for investors to select the most optimal assets considering various portfolio constraints. This paper introduces a model for cardinality-constrained portfolio selection by employing the Golden Eagle Optimizer (GEO) to optimize anticipated returns and the associated risk. To assess the efficacy of the suggested approach, an empirical investigation was carried out by utilizing the three widely recognized benchmark problems (Heng Seng 31, S&P 100, Nikki 225, Dax 100, and FTSE). This involved a performance comparison between the proposed strategy and other contemporary techniques found in the literature. The findings obtained from the study indicate that the GEO approach performs better in addressing large-scale cardinality-constrained portfolio optimization.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Flood Monitoring System Using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This research aims to propose an effective IoT-based flood monitoring system using a machine learning approach (IM-FMS) for flood detection, monitoring and predicting. The proposed methods were demonstrated by using Arduino to collect real-time hydroclimatic data including ambient temperature, relative humidity (RH), Batu River’s water level and rainfall intensity, and then transmit wirelessly to Control Centre by Grove-Wio-E5 LoRa modules through LPWAN communication. Then, every eight seconds, Mosquitto MQTT connection transmits real-time data wirelessly to flood forecasting models, Node-RED IoT dashboard, and saves in local disc without an Internet connection. Node-RED provides a public-accessible and admin-accessible interface for monitoring current weather conditions and modifying subscribers. For data every three minutes, a Wi-Fi connection wirelessly transmits it to Google Spreadsheet for cloud storage. Telegram Bot and email are proposed to send flood alert notifications to respective subscribers. The system’s performance was evaluated in terms of machine learning (ML) models’ results and data transmission range via LoRa. Considering the whole dataset, we can observe that the random forest (RF) model’s accuracy (98.22%), precision (84.00%) and recall rate (70.00%) score are higher than the logistic regression (LR) model’s accuracy (92.74%), precision (29.09%) and recall rate (53.33%) score.

articleTitle: Privacy Preserving Machine Learning Model Personalization through Federated Personalized Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The widespread adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been driven by significant advances in intelligent system research. However, this progress has raised concerns about data privacy, leading to a growing awareness of the need for privacy-preserving AI. In response, there has been a seismic shift in interest towards the leading paradigm for training Machine Learning (ML) models on decentralized data silos while maintaining data privacy, Federated Learning (FL). This research paper presents a comprehensive performance analysis of a cutting-edge approach to personalize ML model while preserving privacy achieved through Privacy Preserving Machine Learning with the innovative framework of Federated Personalized Learning (PPMLFPL). Regarding the increasing concerns about data privacy, this study evaluates the effectiveness of PPMLFPL addressing the critical balance between personalized model refinement and maintaining the confidentiality of individual user data. According to our analysis, Adaptive Personalized Cross-Silo Federated Learning with Differential Privacy (APPLE+DP) offering efficient execution whereas overall, the use of the Adaptive Personalized Cross-Silo Federated Learning with Homomorphic Encryption (APPLE+HE) algorithm for privacy-preserving machine learning tasks in federated personalized learning settings is strongly suggested. The results offer valuable insights creating it a promising scope for future advancements in the field of privacy-conscious data-driven technologies.

articleTitle: Increasing Production Effectiveness: Unveiling the Role of Buffer Inventory in Parallel Machine Scheduling with Machine Breakdowns
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Operational machine status reflects production line efficiency. Increased efficiency is essential for manufacturing systems in the current competitive environment. machine scheduling is critical across manufacturing, parallel computing, and optimization. Customer order scheduling is gaining lot of attention. Real-world systems deal with breakdowns, shifts, instability, aiming for timely production. Parallel machine scheduling involves coordinating machines for performance objectives. Parallel computing complexities grow with problem size. Unrelated parallel machine scheduling is crucial. Batch scheduling for Unrelated Parallel Machine (UPM) faces challenges. Additionally, uncertainties in machine maintenance are indicated by levels, possibly affecting processing time. The role of work in progress (WIP) buffers inventory in uncertain breakdowns is overlooked. This study proposes a method grounded in a job shift system to determine buffer requirements, in stochastics machine maintenance enhancing practical solutions. A mathematical model is developed utilizing CPLEX to address the aforementioned issue. The outcomes demonstrate that the integration of buffer inventory in Parallel Machine Scheduling (PMS) during machine breakdown instances substantially enhances the timely satisfaction of customer orders.

articleTitle: Modelling Nigerian Inflation Rates from January 2003 to June 2023 Using Newly Developed Inverse Power Chi-Square Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: In developing nations like Nigeria, inflation impacts practically every aspect of the economy, and the expenses associated with it are substantial. The severity of the effects of inflation is determined by whether it was expected or unexpected. An expected inflation occurs when households and businesses can consistently forecast the future inflation rate at all times. However, unexpected inflation occurs when they are unable to estimate the future inflation rate. These measures are classified as monetary policy and fiscal policy. The use of statistical models in modelling and forecasting inflation is one of the most recent developments in economic and financial studies. In this study, a new continuous probability distribution is introduced that can be employed to model Nigerias inflation rate from January 2003 to June 2023. The distribution was developed by transforming the chi-square distribution with an additional parameter to unveil the inverse power chi-square distribution. The proposed model has a right and left-skewed form with increasing, constant, and decreasing failure rates, as can be seen from the density shapes. Some statistical properties and parameters of its estimates are examined. It was established that the suggested distribution was the most effective distribution for modeling Nigerias inflation rate.

articleTitle: Fusing Deep Learning and Ensemble Techniques for Comic Character Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Emotions play an essential part in human communication and are tightly entwined with visual storytelling techniques such as comic panel visuals. This research studies the use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) in conjunction with the Random Forest (RF) algorithm for the purpose of accurately classifying the range of emotions that may be found in comic book panels. A carefully selected dataset of 10,000 comic panel images was collected, and it included a spectrum of emotions such as happiness, sadness, rage, surprise, and disgust. The dataset was comprised of carefully picked comic panel images. The hybrid CNN-RF model achieved a great overall accuracy rate of 94.6% after making use of careful preprocessing approaches and carrying out feature extraction. The hybrid technique that was given in this work not only improves the classification of emotions that are depicted in comics, but it also broadens its potential applications in the fields of human-computer interaction, sentiment analysis, and content recommendation systems. The findings highlight the potential for combining art and technology as a tool to convey the many emotional facets that are present in visual narratives. This research presents a vital contribution to the current body of knowledge on emotions within the framework of storytelling, signifying a notable improvement in the field of emotion classification, and it does so by focusing on how emotions are evoked through the medium of narrative.

articleTitle: Exploring Adoption Trends of Knowledge Management Systems in the Software Industry's SMEs: A Comprehensive Investigation of Enablers and Barriers
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The essence of organizational knowledge resides in various aspects of an organization, including processes, products, culture, and systems. Managing this knowledge involves identifying, acquiring, developing, storing, sharing, and evaluating it. Effective knowledge management not only improves an organization's performance but also gives it a competitive advantage. Knowledge Management Systems (KMS), a subset of enterprise systems, help organize and leverage organizational knowledge. Particularly important for Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs), KMS adoption is crucial for their growth. This research focuses on understanding KMS adoption patterns among SMEs in the software industry, using the UTAUT2 framework. The study examines the impact of factors like Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy, Social Influence, and Price Value on users' intention to use KMS. It also explores how Facilitating Conditions and Behavioral Intention affect users' actual usage of KMS. The research follows a quantitative approach, involving an online survey of 383 respondents, with 280 responses analyzed using SPSS. The findings reveal the significant influence of Social Influence on users' behavioral intention to adopt KMS. Additionally, Performance Expectancy and Price Value strongly affect intention, while Effort Expectancy has a positive but weaker impact. Facilitating Conditions and Behavioral Intention are identified as key factors impacting users' KMS usage behavior.

articleTitle: A Holistic Study of Drumstick Leaf Maladies: Leveraging Federated Learning CNN for Improved Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Using Federated Learning combined with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), this study seeks to improve the detection of drumstick leaf disease. The framework includes diverse and location-specific data that includes five kinds of drumstick leaf disease, each represented by five customers. The work combines these disparate data points into a strong global model via federated averaging, substantially contributing to properly diagnosing this prevalent illness. The experimental results provide fascinating new understandings of the behaviour of the combined global model. The Global Accuracy ratings for each customer (V-1 to V-5) ranged from 0.91 for V-1 to an astounding 0.99 for V-5. The average support values for the different clients ranged from 603.20 for V-1 to a maximum of 4640.80 for V-5. While the Weighted Averages exhibited a similar upward trend from 78.18 (V-1) to 97.64 (V-5), the Macro Average metrics among customers ranged from 76.80 (V-1) to 97.34 (V-5). The Micro Averages, representing overall categorization performance, followed the Weighted Averages, with V-1's Micro Average beginning at 78.12 and V-5's Micro Average reaching 97.64. The local models transformed into a single, powerful global model via the creative use of Federated Averaging. It establishes a new paradigm in drumstick leaf disease diagnosis, laying the groundwork for further developments in this crucial area.

articleTitle: A Survey on Cloud Radio Access Network Algorithms for Energy-Efficient Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Cloud Radio Access Network (C-RAN) is considered as a catalyst in increasing energy efficiency in 5G networks by centralizing baseband units that are interconnected to remote radio heads (RRHs). This technology allows to split functions among baseband and radio to significantly optimize performance across the network (lower latency, function offload). However, the C-RAN framework offers several split options, each of which carries specific advantages and disadvantages, when it comes to energy efficiency considerations. In this work, we investigate C-RAN systems in 5G and beyond networks (B5G), with a particular focus on energy efficiency specifications. At first, the study examines the measurable energy-related benefits offered by C-RAN to confirm its importance through operational results. Then, we explore the available C-RAN models in detail, while critically analyzing them, to assess their energy efficiency. The study goes on to discuss the challenges and strategies of choosing the right C-RAN model. Finally, our study concludes that there is no one-size-fits-all approach, when it comes to C-RAN strategies, as their effectiveness depends on variables such as network load, RRH level, energy cost, etc. However, in regard to energy efficiency in B5G, we underline the promising potential of C-RAN to significantly improve the energy efficiency.

articleTitle: The Synergy of Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence in Fintech: Revolutionizing the Financial Landscape
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This paper explores the dynamic interplay between two revolutionary technologies, blockchain and artificial intelligence (AI), and their transformative impact on the realm of financial technology (Fintech). The paper delves into the individual strengths of blockchain and AI and subsequently examines their combined potential in enhancing security, efficiency, and innovation within Fintech. Establishing a strong case for the integration of blockchain and AI as a driving force behind the development of financial services through a thorough study of pertinent literature, case studies, and industry trends.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Techniques for Concrete Compressive Strength Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The compressive strength of concrete is of utmost importance in ensuring the structural stability and integrity of construction projects. With increasing importance placed on this aspect, there is a demand for intelligent and efficient techniques to accurately predict and evaluate compressive strength. Machine learning methods (ML) present a promising approach to developing accurate models for assessing the compressive strength of concrete. By leveraging the power of data analysis and pattern recognition, these techniques enable the construction industry to obtain reliable and robust concrete for a wide range of applications. ML models can identify the key factors influencing compressive strength, allowing for more informed decision-making, and ensuring the construction of structurally sound and durable projects. This article explores the assessment and comparison of four machine learning (ML) methods, namely Gradient Boosting, Categorical Gradient Boosting CatBoost, Random Forest (RF), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) regressors, for predicting concrete compressive strength. Among these techniques, the CatBoost Regressor demonstrated superior performance in terms of accuracy, R-squared coefficient of determination, and Root Mean Square Error RMSE, surpassing the other three methods.

articleTitle: Identification of Risk Control Systems using anchor-words based Correlation Explanation (CorEx) model
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: One of the prominent accident models used to assess risk and hazards in various work systems is the chain of events model, which models the escalation of a hazard into an accident in the form of a chain of sequential activities. To break hazard propagation along the chain, various risk control systems (RCS) need to be developed and implemented at various nodes of the chain. Unfortunately, identification of the RCSs is a tedious and time-consuming process involving manual efforts of subject-matter experts. This paper is an attempt made to use data driven models to identify the RCSs. Using a semi-supervised text mining model called Correlation Explanation (CorEx), we propose a framework that can automate this process of identifying RCSs from incident investigation reports using sets of anchor words. This model shows high applicability of generating multiple hierarchical themes (RCS) from text data without the need of training datasets, thus achieving better interpretability compared to unsupervised topic models while achieving savings in time and effort.

articleTitle: An Optimized Machine Learning Technique for Fault Diagnosis of Roller Bearing in a Motor Drive System
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Early fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) is an essential trait in reducing the maintenance cost and increasing the reliability of the manufacturing system. Considerable advancements have been achieved in recent years toward creating a reliable and automated condition monitoring approach that can detect the occurrence of a fault in advance, permitting the maintenance to be performed proactively to prevent trivial problems from building into catastrophic failures. In this study, we present a radial basis kernel based optimized Support Vector Machine (SVM) for classifying vibrational data obtained from the case western reserve university (CWRU) bearing data set into either good or faulty classes. Instead of using the raw data directly into the model, our method first involves extracting the relevant statistical characteristics from the sensor data. The hyper-parameters C and Gamma of the Support Vector Classifier (SVC) are optimized, resulting in an optimal value that maximizes the accuracy score on both the training and test data. A comprehensive assessment revealed that employing a basic SVM classifier could yield improved accuracy, provided that the features are appropriately extracted and the hyper-parameters are effectively tuned. A distinct demarcation was observed in the majority of the extracted features, resulting in a notable increase in the performance measures. Furthermore, the Fast Fourier Transformation (FFT) was conducted to calculate the Power Spectral Density (PSD) of the signal. This allows for the analysis of the attributes and trends displayed by the data in the frequency domain.

articleTitle: Review previous studies of machine learning techniques to analyze road traffic accidents in different countries
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: RTAs are considered public health issues. For that, many countries and organizations, such as the Gulf Cooperation Council and United Nations, are trying to reduce the number of accidents caused by road traffic. This study reviews several previous studies that used machine learning algorithms to find the best models that can deal with the dataset related to RTAs, it is found the results differentiated by changing the dataset, some high results achieved with the NB algorithm, and the others achieved by using MLP and DT. This study includes more than 30 studies with more than 15 machine learning algorithms. There are several factors that affect the RTAs such as gender driver, age, type of vehicle, cause of accident, and lighting condition. The high number of algorithms used in the previous studies discussed during this study are DT, followed by RF, SVM, and NB respectively. This study provides a review to help researchers to understand the techniques used to analyze the dataset in the RTA sector.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Intrusion Detection System in the Internet of Things Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: With billions of interconnected devices on the Internet, the Internet of Things (IoT) has emerged as a fundamental facet of our daily existence, influencing everything from our lifestyles to our work routines. This massive connectivity of devices to the Internet has put IoT systems at risk of cyber-attacks. The integration of IoT devices into various verticals has brought about unseen opportunities and challenges as well. There exists a need for robust as well as efficient Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) keeping in view the growing complexity of IoT networks. IDS plays a pivotal role in safeguarding the IoT environment by identifying malicious activities. In addition to traditional IDS approaches, contemporary approaches face challenges in effectively identifying the dynamic IoT network traffic as normal or malicious. To deal with this, we propose a novel hybrid deep learning classification model (CNN-LSTM), tailored specifically for IoT-based IDS. The proposed CNN-LSTM model capitalizes on the characteristics of both CNN and LSTM architectures. Our study employs a benchmark dataset, IoT-23 to train and evaluate the CNN-LSTM model. The dataset is first pre-processed, followed by feature selection by means of the Chi-Square Test. Finally, the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is applied to balance the dataset before training the proposed model. The experimental findings showcase that our proposed model surpasses accuracies achieved by Logistic Regression, Naïve Bayes, CNN, LSTM models, and other existing models, achieving an impressive accuracy of 99.98%. By tapping into the power of deep learning, this model demonstrates outstanding potential in efficiently securing IoT networks from cyber-attacks leading to the construction of safe and reliable IoT ecosystems. In conclusion, the proposed model displays robustness against previously unseen intrusion patterns, illustrating its ability to respond to evolving cyber threats in the dynamic IoT world.

articleTitle: Bagging Machine Learning Classifier Model to Predict Diabetes Mellitus Disease
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Today, diabetes mellitus is one of the diseases with the greatest global mortality and morbidity contributions and is also one of the fastest rising. In order to recognize the existence of diabetes mellitus early on, a variety of sophisticated methods incorporating machine learning have been developed. However, most methods have produced results with comparably less accuracy. The focus of this study is on establishing a machine learning-based system for early detection of diabetes risk in patients. This research work has employed a bagging classifier and dataset sample, which includes both positive as well as negative test results for individual patients. The performance has been evaluated using precision, recall, accuracy, F1-score, ROC-AUC, sensitivity, or specificity. The proposed model produces the most reliable results for predicting diabetes, and results demonstrate that the prediction system can instantly predict diabetes disease.

articleTitle: Securing Business Intelligence during Mergers and Acquisition: Critical Cybersecurity Imperatives
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: In today's business world, cybersecurity in M&A is a significant problem. There is not much research done in the context of problems associated with the adoption and effectiveness of Business Intelligence systems. M&A and technological innovation are rapidly shifting economic dynamics that have forced companies to reevaluate their approach and use Business intelligence systems, and with that comes the risk of cyber-attacks. This paper explains how M&A can be impacted when there is a failure in cyber security assessment and why the organization faces cyber security beaches during M&A. Analysis of cyber security risk in mergers and acquisition life cycle concerning time. This paper is a stepby-step guide to the key cybersecurity framework of Secure, Vigilant, and Resilient for pre-merger to the post-merger merger of an M&A explained at the subsequent phases. Also, the traditional way for mergers and acquisitions is outdated, and adopting the modern cyber security assessment is mandatory during mergers and acquisitions. This paper covers an action guide for cyber security assessment for mergers and acquisitions. Therefore, business owners must prioritize it because failing to do so will work against the business.

articleTitle: Digital Twins for Healthcare and Telecommunications Applications: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Being a virtual model, designed to accurately reflect a physical object, Digital Twins (DTs) are gaining a lot of attention, nowadays. Indeed, by providing a virtual copy of a living or a non-living entity, DTs have revolutionized various domains by allowing seamless simulations, facilitating decision-making, and predicting the need for maintenance to name a few use-cases. The advancements of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and the Internet of Things (IoT) have resulted in significant improvements in DTs. However, despite a noticeable adoption in the fields of education, and Industry 4.0, DT is still at its early stages in the health and telecommunications domains. Therefore, in this paper, we comprehensively review the state-of-the-art of DTs in terms of technologies, applications, challenges and future directions with a focus on these two domains. Particularly, we investigate the advantages of integrating ML in the DT ecosystem. Moreover, we synthesize current approaches by providing a workflow comparison of trending DT-related research questions. Accordingly, when analyzing enablers for DTs, we concluded that some challenges need to be addressed such as data privacy, reliability, and scalability to enable further adoption of the DT in the real-world. We thoroughly discuss these before elaborating our views on future directions.

articleTitle: Classification of brain ischemia and hemorrhagic stroke using a hybrid method
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: The availability of artificial intelligence applications has expanded with the development of extremely powerful computers. This speeds up the diagnosis of many ailments and allows for the application of effective treatments. This facilitates the work of numerous experts in the field of health, and more trustworthy outcomes are attained. Many researchers have started working in this topic as a result of how swiftly artificial intelligence has entered human life and the promising outcomes that have been obtained. The detection of brain strokes from CT images, which are the most prevalent in the world and a major threat to human life, is a field that is currently seeing a flurry of deep learning and machine learning-based approaches. This study attempted to distinguish between ischemic and hemorrhagic brain stroke types using CT images. Utilizing a hybrid methodology, multi-classification was carried out utilizing EfficientNetB0 and SVM model from ischemic, hemorrhagic, and normal brain CT images in our dataset. The purpose of this study is to demonstrate a higher classification performance by combining the feature extraction skills of deep learning networks with the classification capability of machine learning models. The ischemic, hemorrhagic, and normal CT images in our dataset were used to train the EfficientNet-B0 + SVM, EfficientNet-B0 + KNN, ResNet50 + SVM, ResNet50 + KNN, ResNet50, VGG19 + SVM, VGG19 + KNN, and VGG19 models. There was a triple classification. According to the study, the hybrid EfficientNet-B0 + SVM architecture had the highest load success rate. The model had 95.13%, 94.93, 95.06, and 94.94% accuracy, recall, precision, and F1 values, respectively. These findings demonstrated that the EfficientNet-B0 + SVM architecture is a highly effective method for classifying different types of brain strokes from CT images.

articleTitle: Agricultural Revitalization through Federated Learning CNN in Data Analytics: A Case Study on Drumstick Leaf Disease
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This study uses Federated Learning combined with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to diagnose and categorize drumstick leaf disease in a novel way. This multi-centric study involved five clients, each representing a unique subset of drumstick leaf conditions. The Federated Learning methodology received excellent marks for generalizability and respected data privacy. Impressive metrics were used in the result analysis to identify five separate classes of drumstick leaf diseases: g-1 (80.69%), g-2 (83.41%), g-3 (83.18%), g-4 (86.75%), and g-5 (86.05%) for individual accuracies. These regional data sets were combined via federated averaging, and the resulting Macro, Micro, and Weighted averages were 80.51%, 81.87%, and 81.81%, respectively. By using federated learning, a generalizable approach whose effectiveness has been proven by the constant performance across different clients, our work introduces a fresh paradigm for data privacy. These privacy-protection strategies may easily be used in various industries, meeting moral and practical requirements. Unquestionably, data analytics plays a crucial role in contemporary agriculture. The model's high accuracy levels (e.g., a weighted average of 84.30% for client g-2) closely match the operational objectives of modern agricultural firms, demonstrating the paper's applicability to the conference's subject of improving business operations. A more considerable economic debate is crucial, too. The data shows that optimum agricultural practices may be possible if disease categorization is consistent and accurate. Scaling up these methods will significantly affect economic development, with products that go beyond agriculture and into industries like supply chain management and healthcare. The study demonstrates significant progress in using federated learning with CNN for detecting agricultural diseases, establishing the groundwork for future multidisciplinary studies that address data privacy, operational effectiveness, and economic development.

articleTitle: CT Image-Based Lung Cancer Detection Using a CNN-Based Model
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: One of the most prevalent cancers worldwide is lung cancer which contributes to cancer-related death. Smoking is mostly responsible for lung cancer. Existing lung cancer detection methods involve using numerous medical imaging procedures like X-ray, CT scan, and MRI, combined with machine learning algorithms for accurate diagnosis. Some of the current research on lung cancer detection has limitations in terms of accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. More research is required to enhance precise detection. In this study, we used the "IQ-OTH/NCCD - Lung Cancer Dataset" sourced from Kaggle and proposed an XceptionNet based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture for the precise detection of lung cancer using CT images. The proposed Xception model achieved a higher accuracy of 99.64% and a lower loss compared to existing models and showed that it could be used to better accurately diagnose lung cancer from CT scans. We contrasted our model with other baseline models.

articleTitle: Using Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Mammogram ROI Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: This paper explores the use of cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for identifying cancerous cells in annotated regions of interest in mammogram images with the goal of early detection and treatment which is key to reducing the risk of cancer development and death. Our proposed MARL model deploys multiple agents on mammogram images that collaboratively scan and communicate observations with other agents to extract features in a decentralized fashion and classify ROI patches as benign or malignant. As opposed to processing whole images at a time, partial observations by agents result in decreased computational complexity. The achieved accuracy, precision, and recall of our architecture on the CBIS-DDSM (mass) dataset were 82.45%, 81.73% and 81.00% respectively.

articleTitle: The Influence of Social Media Marketing Elements on Consumer Brand Engagement and Its Impact on Brand Awareness and Brand Image
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Social media marketing is a powerful tool for businesses to engage with consumers and build brand awareness and image. This study investigates the impact of social media marketing elements, namely entertainment, customization, interaction, EWOM, and trends, on consumer brand engagement and brand awareness in the smartphone industry. An online survey used to collect data from 185 experienced social media users finds that customization, interaction, EWOM, and trendy content are the critical social media marketing elements that influence consumer brand engagement, which leads to increased brand awareness and brand image. The findings can help marketers develop more effective social media marketing campaigns to enhance consumer brand engagement, brand awareness, and brand image.
